bottom_line_fact.text: SemiAnalysis's parcel-level audit finds that 300+ local moratoriums and NY's order delay only ~2.3GW genuinely, with just 1,525 MW (7.6% of restricted-boundary capacity) delayed at the local level, against a +38GW 2027 US delivery forecast.

bottom_line_inference.text: The moratorium narrative appears materially overstated as a near-term risk to datacenter capacity and the AI infrastructure supply chain, though the article quantifies no specific listed-company earnings or revenue effect.

disconfirming_observables: A sharp rise in enacted statewide moratoriums reaching floor votes
Revocation (not just freezing) of already-granted datacenter approvals
Upward revision to SemiAnalysis's genuinely-delayed GW estimate

near_term_view.text: For all of 2026 and most of 2027, moratoriums are out of reach of capacity already under construction or permitted, so near-term delivery is largely protected.

hypotheses.next_research_step: Cross-check SemiAnalysis's ~2.3GW delayed estimate and 2027 +38GW delivery forecast against hyperscaler capex guidance and datacenter REIT/supplier backlog disclosures to see if any earnings effect is implied.

opposing_explanations.text: The widespread media narrative holds that moratoriums are killing the US datacenter buildout, legislated to a halt one board at a time.
Public sentiment is significantly negative on datacenters (46% unfavorable) and could intensify opposition, potentially widening restrictions over time.

raise_priority_if: Statewide moratorium bills begin passing floor votes
SemiAnalysis raises its genuinely-delayed GW estimate in bi-weekly updates

sector_exposures.name: datacenters
sector_exposures.quote: +38GW of Datacenter IT capacity delivered in the US in 2027

source_implication.text: The article concludes the buildout is not being legislated to a halt; capacity under construction or permitted for 2026 and most of 2027 is out of reach of moratoriums.

structural_view.text: SemiAnalysis maintains moratoriums could delay the buildout only if they become materially more widespread and restrictive.

hypotheses.title: Datacenter moratoriums barely dent the US AI buildout pipeline

transmission_chain.text: Hundreds of local moratoriums and four state actions are raising political/regulatory friction for datacenter development.
Parcel-level analysis shows only ~2.3GW genuinely delayed, so delivered datacenter capacity (+38GW in 2027) is largely unaffected.
Would imply datacenter capex/revenue for hyperscalers and suppliers proceeds roughly on plan, but the article quantifies no earnings effect.

unknowns: Whether moratoriums become materially more widespread and restrictive, which the article says would be needed to delay the buildout
Whether any listed hyperscaler or datacenter supplier earnings/revenue actually change as a result
Whether the parcel-level exposure-vs-delay mapping holds for 2028+ projects not yet permitted

bottom_line_fact.text: Texas's ERCOT queue pause adds only 3-4 months for base-load projects but is offset by acceleration of behind-the-meter demand; SemiAnalysis counted 75GW of firm BtM equipment orders (most for Texas) and forecasts BtM powering more than half of new US capacity from 2028.

bottom_line_inference.text: Grid interconnection friction appears to be a net positive for behind-the-meter and on-site generation equipment suppliers, though the article names no listed company exposed to it.

catalyst.window_text: from 2028 (BtM powering more than half of new capacity)

disconfirming_observables: Grid interconnection timelines accelerate, reducing BtM demand
Cancellation of firm BtM equipment orders
lower_priority_if: BtM share of new capacity falls below forecast

near_term_view.text: Texas grid pause adds only 3-4 months administrative delay for base-load projects, offset by BtM acceleration.

hypotheses.next_research_step: Identify the listed gas turbine, gensets and on-site power equipment suppliers capturing the 75GW of firm BtM orders and check order backlogs skewed to Texas.
raise_priority_if: Firm BtM equipment orders rise above 75GW
More states pause grid interconnection queues

sector_exposures.name: behind-the-meter power / on-site generation suppliers
sector_exposures.quote: making it a net positive for BtM developers and on-site generation suppliers

source_implication.text: The audit reinforces SemiAnalysis's view that the buildout is moving behind-the-meter, a net positive for BtM developers and on-site generation suppliers.

structural_view.text: The buildout is structurally moving behind-the-meter, with BtM forecast to power more than half of new US datacenter capacity from 2028.

hypotheses.title: Grid friction pushes datacenters behind-the-meter, benefiting on-site generation suppliers

transmission_chain.text: Grid interconnection pauses and energization-at-meter restrictions push developers toward behind-the-meter power.
75GW of firm BtM equipment orders placed and BtM forecast to power over half of new US capacity from 2028, raising demand for on-site generation equipment.
Would imply higher volumes/revenue for on-site generation suppliers, but the article names no listed supplier and quantifies no earnings effect.

unknowns: Which listed companies supply the 75GW of firm BtM equipment orders
Whether on-site generation economics earn a return relative to grid power
Whether the BtM share forecast (>half from 2028) is realized

market_risks.scope_qualification: US voter sentiment per SemiAnalysis's August 2026 Tokenomics survey; the article says moratoriums are not yet at scale but could delay the buildout if they become more widespread.
market_risks.statement: Public sentiment is significantly negative on datacenters (46% unfavorable, 46% would oppose one locally), and SemiAnalysis warns this gap could widen with AI doomsday narratives, potentially making moratoriums materially more widespread and restrictive.

market_risks.scope_qualification: US state and local campaigns; the article frames this as a catalyst for new restrictions rather than an established delay to capacity.
market_risks.statement: Election-year politics (November 2026 midterms) could raise the political cost of approving datacenter projects, as candidates like Vivek Ramaswamy pledge strict conditions, potentially catalyzing new restrictions.
